title: Understand and Use Standard Deviation
description: Interpret standard deviation as spread, compare data sets conceptually, predict how changing values affects spread, and calculate standard deviation with Desmos.

questions.stem_html: Which set has a greater standard deviation? Set A is [13, 16, 19]. Set B is [10, 16, 22].
questions.explanation_html: Both means are 16. The outer values in B are twice as far from the mean as the outer values in A.
questions.variation: Compare sets with the same mean and different spread

questions.stem_html: Which set has a greater standard deviation? Set A is [6, 8, 10]. Set B is [21, 23, 25].
questions.explanation_html: Each value moves by 15, and so does the mean. The distances from each mean are identical.

questions.stem_html: A data set is [18, 20, 22]. The value 34 is added. What happens to the population standard deviation?
questions.explanation_html: The new value is far from all three originals and increases their average squared distance from the mean.
questions.variation: Compare spread before and after adding or removing an outlier

questions.stem_html: A data set is [11, 13, 15, 25]. Its largest value is replaced by 13. What happens to the population standard deviation?
questions.explanation_html: The replacement turns the distant value into a central value, reducing the spread.
questions.variation: Evaluate the effect of replacing an outlier

questions.stem_html: The sample consists of 14, 18, and 22. What is its sample standard deviation?
questions.explanation_html: The mean is 18 and the squared deviations sum to 32. For a sample divide by 3 − 1, then take the positive square root.
